ev.q: The risk for hepatitis A among close personal contacts of international adoptees is estimated at 106 (range: 90--819) per 100,000 household contacts
Since 2007, CDC has received 14 additional reports of acute hepatitis A following exposure to nonjaundiced adoptees
This same study found that 98% of parents traveling to pick up their children had been vaccinated against hepatitis A
indicate that 1%--6% of newly arrived international adoptees are acutely infected with HAV
the estimated rate of symptomatic hepatitis A in the U.S. general population in 2007 was 1.0 per 100,000 population
ACIP updated its guidance by recommending hepatitis A vaccination for all previously unvaccinated persons
This case prompted further investigation that led to identification of 20 other cases
contact with an international adoptee is not asked routinely as part of national hepatitis A surveillance

methods_quotes.q: Data from a study conducted at three adoption clinics in the United States, each screening 100--200 incoming adoptees for hepatitis A each year
